summary.name: Making the most of an SRE service takeover
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud Blog article (part 3 of a series) describing how SRE teams prepare for, take over, and sometimes hand back a service's on-call pager from developers.
keywords: take the pager for a spin
use_cases: Preparing a team to take on on-call for a developer-owned service
Measuring whether an SRE handover succeeded
Deciding when to hand the pager back to developers
Reducing SRE toil after a service takeover
Improving collaboration between developers and SRE teams
summary.what_it_does: The article walks through the onboarding phase after an SRE team agrees to support a service: education sessions, a week of sharing pager alerts scored on criticality and actionability, and on-call shadowing with developers. It suggests success criteria for a handover, such as fewer pages and outages, reduced deployment toil, and better resource utilization. It gives a timeline for taking over the pager (a hitlist of toil reduction over one to two months, and meeting success measures over three to six months). It also covers handing the pager back when paging load becomes excessive, with an example of a data-driven message to developers.
notable: Pager handover timeline: one to two months for a toil hitlist, three to six months to meet success criteria
Alerts scored on criticality and actionability during a one-week trial
Describes handing the pager back when paging load gets too high, or when a new service version replaces an old one
caveats: Describes Google's internal SRE practice; it is not a tool or product, and the page does not present a specific software product.
